request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Pick the configuration to carry forward. Use fold-level evidence to decide: a config that wins a majority of folds is more trustworthy than one with a higher mean but inconsistent fold performance. Between two configs with similar fold-win rates, prefer the simpler model. Flag any result that looks too good. You may request up to 0 more round(s) of experiments; set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. Rate your confidence in chosen_run (0-1): 1.0 means one config clearly wins most folds and no reasonable reviewer would disagree; 0.5 means fold wins are split roughly evenly or something looks off. You can inspect the per-fold PR-AUC breakdown of any completed run. Compare fold-by-fold: count how many folds each config wins to assess which is genuinely better vs lucky. (Independent run 2.)

concerns: Run 6 wins 3 of 5 folds against run 4 (folds 1, 3, 4). Run 4 wins fold 2 by 0.0028 and fold 5 by 0.0030. Run 3 wins fold 4 outright (0.8069 vs 0.8026). Margins are small, with a mean gap of about 0.004 against a fold SD of about 0.06, so the lead is not statistically meaningful.
Run 6 beats run 1 in all 5 folds and run 3 in 4 of 5, so its edge over the default LightGBM config is consistent, but the absolute gain is tiny.
Fold 3 is weak for every config (0.62-0.64) and fold SD is about 0.06, so fold-to-fold variance dominates config differences. Fold composition or temporal drift may be responsible.

The PotentialFraud label has an undocumented origin and is only a suspicion signal. High ROC-AUC (about 0.946) and PR-AUC of about 0.74 may reflect label-generating proxies such as volume or size features rather than true fraud, so audit yield is not guaranteed.
Precision at k=50 is flat at about 0.78 across the LightGBM configs. The audit queue is about 100, and there is no precision at 100 evidence, so queue-level performance is uncertain.
The agent feature set adds only a small gain (run 4 vs run 1: +0.004, 3 of 5 folds), so it is modest and may be noise. The features' provenance should be checked for leakage.
The search was narrow (6 configs, no logistic baseline, no SMOTE), and only runs 1, 3, 4 and 6 had fold detail inspected. Run 2 and run 5 were not examined, but their means are lower.
